Valrasian

Overview

Valrasian governs the Ingos city and collects curiosities. He presents himself as an enlightened ruler and takes an interest in Kel and the visitors’ discoveries. In the murder investigation he demands evidence before accepting Crooked’s guilt, asks why his court magician His died and seeks the return of his stolen nugget. [1, 2]

Yam-Akara’s research and the governor’s gift

Yam-Akara introduces himself as a practising magician of the first rank and an honorary member of the Assembly of Magicians of Three Worlds. The elemental samples interest him, and the Joon artifact promises material for a scholarly report. He agrees to search while Kir renews his permit for the mines, where Wormface magic interferes with his measurements. His summons the travellers to Governor Valrasian whether or not his own laboratory errand is complete. The governor demands proper introductions, pays unwelcome attention to Kel and hints at a rare Blue Clan mage’s dart for his collection. Bringing the dart wins the permit, despite his complaints about Yam-Akara’s visits. [3, 4, 5, 6, 1, 7, 8]

Brissen’s murder and the failed alibi

Green leaves around the settlement lead Kir to Grey Leaf, who brings the news. Brissen is murdered and Yam-Akara is accused of killing his old friend. Kir and Kel undertake the defence. The magician says he spent the day in the mines and arrived late for their meeting. Soldier confirms that he allowed the elderly visitor through with an expired permit and stamped it that day. Kir finds the lost pass, but Valrasian rejects the water-damaged document because the signature and date can no longer be read. This evidence supports the search but does not free Yam-Akara; the travellers still have to identify the murderer. [9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15]

The planted knife and His’s death

A knife found at the murder site appears to implicate His. The court magician admits it was stolen from his laboratory together with the governor’s nugget. He had sent out the empty caravan to hide that loss and hoped to blame raiders after an informant warned of the planned attack. His arranges a meeting to produce evidence, but is killed before he can clear himself. Meanwhile Geraldine and Karansul disclose their relationship and provide each other with an alibi. Their commercial hostility and private secrecy had made them suspicious without establishing guilt. [16, 17, 18, 19, 20]

Crooked’s confession

The settlement’s missing communal money supplies the decisive motive. Kir and Kel catch Crooked at his cache. Brissen had discovered the theft, so Crooked killed him. He also stole His’s knife and the gold nugget, informed on the caravan raid and later planted the knife to shift suspicion. His called the same informant to clear his own name; Crooked mistook that invitation for a trap and killed him too. Woodsfolk observations help reconstruct the planted evidence. Before the governor, Kir explains the connected crimes and Crooked admits them. Yam-Akara is released, while the governor reserves Crooked’s punishment for trial. Kel draws the thief out by spreading word that they have found the hidden money. Afterwards the travellers return the recovered communal funds to Geraldine and Trickster. Geraldine wants personal revenge, but Crooked is already in the governor’s custody. [21, 22, 23, 24, 2, 25, 26]
